newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria to peg lev to mark at 1,000 July 1-FinMin.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria to peg lev to mark at 1,000 July 1-FinMin.

text.p: Bulgaria's Finance Minister Muravei Radev said on Tuesday that cabinet will propose to peg the lev to the mark at a fixed exchange rate of 1,000 from July 1 when a currency board system is to be launched.
"The cabinet will propose to use the German mark as an anchor in a currency board arrangement at a rate of 1,000 levs per mark," Radev told a news conference.
He also said this year's projected GDP is 16.15 trillion levs in a draft budget which has yet to be approved by cabinet and parliament by end-June.
Radev said the cabinet will propose to parliament to include the mark/lev peg as an article in the new central bank law due to be voted on final reading on Wednesday or Thursday.
Parliament will be expected to announce that this fixed exchange rate will become effective on July 1 when the currency board is launched, said Radev.
Bulgaria will enter the currency board arrangement with issue department reserves of around $1 billion, said IMF team leader Anne McGuirk.
Under a currency board system recommended by the IMF to stabilise Bulgaria's economy levs in circulation must be exactly matched by central bank issue department foreign exchange reserves.
Assumed revenue in this year's budget was seen at 27.3 percent of GDP, expenses at 33.5 percent of GDP.
The budget deficit was assumed at 6.2 percent of GDP, higher than IMF-recommended 3.8 percent due to pending interest payments on Bulgarian foreign and domestic debt.
An average lev/dollar exchange rate of 1,700 was assumed in the 1997 budget. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
